Mysterious Off-Road-Ready Test Mule Spied, Could It Be Audi’s Mercedes G-Class Rival?
10 photos
Photo: SH Proshots
While the Volkswagen Group is struggling financially and some upcoming products have been put on ice for now, the automotive giant appears to be preparing a very interesting vehicle as we speak, and if it is indeed what we said in the title, then it will be one very special ride.
First things first, these images just ended up in our inboxes sent by our spy photographers, who immortalized this mysterious test mule somewhere in Europe, at an Audi facility. The location is said to be “extremely confidential and sensitive,” which is why they have removed the background in order to “protect the exact location and our sources.” And now you know why this thing appears to be floating in the air next to a leafless tree.
Our man with the cam also noted that the camouflage is not typical for Audi , but then again, this is no ordinary machine either. It has been clearly built for some serious off-roading, hence the large ground clearance, and the six-lug wheels shod in BFGoodrich all-terrain tires. It has a light bar on the roof, some sturdy side steps, fender flares, and this is basically where everything that we know about it ends and the speculation begins.
Thus, as we said in the title, there is a chance that we are indeed looking at Audi’s rival to the likes of the Mercedes G-Wagen. This thing has been brought into discussion for the past couple of years or so, though it seems that it was eventually forgotten. To be honest, this might not be a great time to develop such a thing, as it definitely eats a huge amount of money poured into the research and development, and not only, but it appears to be a bet that the four-ring brand has already placed.
Photo: SH Proshots Mind you, there is no clear indication that we are indeed looking at the Mercedes G-Class rival from Audi , as even our spies are not entirely convinced. In fact, they have said that it could be a test mule of the future Volkswagen Touareg, too. However, we wouldn’t bet on it, because the six-lug wheels do not seem like a logical approach for such a thing. Then again, they definitely fit the nature of a real off-road from Audi.
Audi themselves, through the voice of CEO Gernot Dollner, suggested that the SUV in question might share quite a few things with Scout’s new models, namely the Terra and the Traveler. The latter is an SUV, whereas the former is a pickup. And guess what? Both feature six-lug wheels, just like this mysterious tester that recently became the focus of our spy photographer’s camera lens.
The company’s head honcho said that a body-on-frame SUV is “ in the framework, ” although he admitted that “ no decision has been taken yet, ” adding that “ if we do something like that, it is only thinkable to do it on a platform that is already there. ” Scout’s Terra and Traveler were unveiled in the United States of America last year, and will be put together locally starting from 2027.
If you think that Audi’s potential upcoming G-Wagen rival might be offered with gasoline power, perhaps with a V8 being part of the offering, then you are wrong. That’s because the Scout models are fully electric, with dual-motor setups and full-time four-wheel drive. Moreover, they also feature a ladder-frame construction, as well as locking differentials at the front and rear.
Photo: SH Proshots However, given that EVs are not exactly popular in some parts of the world, we would not be surprised to learn that Audi might shift its strategy when it comes to the Mercedes G-Wagen competitor . And if that happens, then it will be interesting to learn whether the platform might be modified to support ICE power. If the answer is yes, then there is a chance that the Scouts might also get ICE units, though this is pure speculation at this point, so you may want to take it with a pinch of salt.
By the way, let’s not forget that the Mercedes G-Wagen also comes with EV power. The model is called the Mercedes-Benz G 580, features four permanently synchronous electric motors, has 579 hp (432 kW/587 ps) and 859 pound-feet (1,165 Nm) of torque in total, and completes the 0-60 mph (0-97 kph) in 4.6 seconds. And it’s not exactly that popular, in case you forgot.
It’s not only the Mercedes-Benz G-Class and its range-topping version, the Mercedes- AMG G 63, that will be targeted by the Audi off-roader, but also the Land Rover Defender. BMW is also reportedly working on such a thing. The project is codenamed the G74, and could be a bit milder, as it is expected to utilize the versatile CLAR construction, albeit perhaps with a few modifications.
What’s your take on the fact that Audi and BMW are both interested in launching some off-road-oriented models? And could this test mule actually offer an initial glimpse into the four-ring brand’s upcoming 4x4?
